Supplement

/SUP-luh-ment/ — starts like 'supper' · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To supplement to build something up by adding an extra amount or piece to it.

Farmers supplement the poor soil with compost to help the crops thrive.

Worked Example

Marcus loved his history textbook, but it barely covered ancient trade routes. So he added documentaries, museum visits, and a podcast to his study routine, layering extra sources on top of the book.

Marcus supplemented his textbook — he enhanced it by adding extra elements. To 'replace' the book would mean discarding it; to supplement it means keeping it and adding more on top.

How Supplement Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

augment

augment: to make greater by adding to it

bolster

bolster: to strengthen or support with additions

enrich: to improve the quality of by adding something

Antonyms

reduce

reduce: to make smaller or less

deplete

deplete: to use up or drain away

How Strong Is It? — tweak → supplement → transform

tweak vs. supplement

tweak vs. supplement: Tweak is weaker than supplement — a tweak changes only a tiny detail, while supplementing adds a whole extra element.

transform vs. supplement

transform vs. supplement: Transform is stronger than supplement — supplementing adds to what's already there, but transforming changes the thing completely.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — sup- (sub-)

prefix — sup- (sub-): up from below (Latin)

root — ple-

root — ple-: to fill (Latin)

suffix — -ment

suffix — -ment: result or means of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin supplere meant 'to fill up from below.' To supplement is to pour more in — filling up what is lacking until something is fuller and better.
